security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-focused, but it intentionally demonstrates network, environment, filesystem, and external-command operations. Most severe detector matches are syntax or prose false positives; privileged archive extraction and shell evaluation of credential output remain high-risk guidance. Static review was capped at 400/668 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 268 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The Linux installer pipes a downloaded archive directly into sudo tar.
remediation.suggestion: Download to a temporary file, verify a published checksum or signature, inspect the archive, then install the verified binary with limited privileges.

remediation.suggestion: Provide shell-escaped exports from the CLI or parse dotenv output without eval. Keep tokens out of logs and command histories.

content.value_statement: Claude API details change across models, SDKs, and platforms. This skill provides current, language-specific guidance for implementation, migration, authentication, and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Selects current Claude model identifiers and explains supported capabilities.
Provides Anthropic SDK examples for Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, PHP, Ruby, C#, and curl.
Guides streaming, tool use, structured outputs, files, batches, and token counting.
Explains API key, OAuth profile, cloud platform, and workload identity authentication.
Documents managed agents, environments, sessions, memory, webhooks, and scheduled deployments.
Maps older Claude API patterns to current request parameters and SDK methods.
limitations: Examples require valid Anthropic credentials and may create billable API usage.
Beta endpoints and model capabilities can change after the skill is published.
Some examples read local files, environment variables, or credential profiles.
The skill does not provision cloud accounts, credentials, or production infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Create a Claude API prototype
use_cases.description: Generate a minimal request with the correct SDK, model identifier, authentication, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing integration
use_cases.description: Update deprecated model identifiers, thinking parameters, tools, and retry behavior for current Claude models.

use_cases.title: Design a managed agent workflow
use_cases.description: Plan agents, environments, sessions, resources, memory, events, and deployment controls for an operational workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Send a first message
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal Claude API request in [language] that sends [message] and prints the response.

prompt_templates.title: Add streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my [language] Claude request to stream text, handle errors, and report final token usage.

prompt_templates.title: Implement tool use
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Claude tool loop for [task] in [language], including validation, tool results, iteration limits, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a production integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [project or file] and migrate its Claude integration to [target model], preserving behavior, tests, observability, caching, and retry controls.

output_examples.input: Create a Python request that summarizes support tickets with Claude.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering client initialization, model selection, message construction, error handling, and token usage.

output_examples.input: Explain why my streaming tool loop stops after the first tool call.
output: The likely control-flow cause and the relevant stop reason.
A corrected loop sequence with validation and iteration limits.
Checks for malformed tool results and partial stream events.

output_examples.input: Plan a managed agent that reviews repositories every weekday.
output_examples.output: An architecture covering the agent, environment, repository resource, credentials, session lifecycle, schedule, observability, and failure recovery.

best_practices: Use the official SDK for the project language and verify current model identifiers.
Keep credentials in approved secret stores and grant only required scopes.
Add timeouts, retry limits, validation, logging, and cost monitoring before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not invent model identifiers, SDK methods, or beta header versions.
Do not print credentials or place long-lived secrets in source files.
Do not run unbounded tool loops or trust tool inputs and outputs without validation.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, PHP, Ruby, C#, and direct curl requests.

faq.question: Does it provide current Claude model identifiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a model reference and migration guidance, but live availability should still be verified.

faq.question: Can it help with tool use and MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains tool schemas, execution loops, server tools, MCP connections, validation, and common failures.

faq.question: Does it require an Anthropic API key?
faq.answer: It requires a supported credential source, such as an API key, OAuth profile, or configured cloud identity.

faq.question: Can it migrate an existing Claude integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps older models and request patterns to current SDK and API behavior.

faq.question: Does it execute API calls automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance and examples. Execution depends on the host agent, available tools, credentials, and user authorization.
